comment.narrative: In February 2021, Dutch parliament accepted a motion which calls on the Dutch government to promote in the EU that pharmaceutical companies will share their knowledge on corona vaccines via C-TAP and sub-license their patents to as many suitable producers as possible. In March 2021, political party SP submits parliamentary questions about attaching conditions to public investments in drug development to ensure affordability and accessibility of drugs or vaccines.

In October 2022 Dutch minister Schreinemacher made a public statement that she wants a thorough revision of the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises. The Netherlands supports explicitly mentioning the safety of human rights defenders in the OECD Guidelines, as is in line with the Dutch human rights policy. In 2023, a member of parliament asked critical questions on how it was possible that pharmaceutical companies could make large profits from the Corona vaccination. In 2022, the Netherlands Court of Audit includes SOMO input on attaching conditions to public funding of medicines and vaccines in their evaluation framework.

description.narrative: Cases of changed (inter)national expectations of whether (inter)national trade and value chains should safeguard peoples' rights, and -if so- how

comment.narrative: In June 2022 the OECD has started a process to go through targeted updates to the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises, which could potentially strengthen responsible business conduct standards regarding human rights defenders, land rights, corp In December 2022, the European Council has adopted its negotiating position ('general approach') on the corporate sustainability due diligence directive (CSDDD). In February 2022, the European Commission has published its proposal for a Directive on corporate sustainability due diligence (CSDDD), which, after revision, could represent a landmark step forward in the direction of minimising the negative impacts of businesses on workers, communities and the environment worldwide, and advancing corporate accountability and justice. On 1 November 2022, six Dutch political parties (ChristenUnie, D66, PvdA, GroenLinks, SP, Volt) have formally submitted their Bill on Responsible and Sustainable International Business Conduct to the Dutch House of Representatives, in an effort to oblige enterprises to conduct business with respect for human rights, the environment, and the climate in accordance with the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises. In its coalition agreement, published January 2022, the Dutch government agreed to develop due diligence legislation to promote for responsible business conduct by companies abroad. In September 2022 the Dutch government has published its new National Plan Plan (NAP) on Business and Human Rights 2022-2026. The action plan clearly outlines action points for the responsible ministries, including a number of new actions to improve access to remedy for victims of corporate-related human rights abuses."
